findings.body: **`Allow-Origin: *` with credentials is invalid, and native clients ignore CORS.** When `origin` is null this emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, which browsers must reject per the Fetch CORS rules. Native mobile HTTP clients do not enforce CORS at all, so this fallback does not unlock them. Prefer keeping credentials only for allowlisted browser origins; leave non-browser callers outside the CORS path.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical CORS regression: this change turns a fixed allowlist into a credentialed reflect-any-origin policy, which lets any website read authenticated API responses in the browser.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `src/middleware/cors.ts:4` | Reflects arbitrary `Origin` with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `src/middleware/cors.ts:4` | `origin ?? "*"` plus credentials is invalid per CORS and does not help native clients |

## Notes

CORS is enforced by browsers only. Native mobile HTTP stacks do not consult `Access-Control-*` headers, so loosening CORS is the wrong lever for “mobile clients.” If the real need is mobile *webviews* on known hosts, extend the allowlist (or a verified pattern) for those origins instead of reflecting every caller.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
